title: Internal cyclotron probe of the vertical polarizability of a surface-state electron on helium
abstract: We study a surface-state electron on liquid helium in a tilted magnetic field. The tilt couples the cyclotron ladder to the vertical Rydberg-like subbands of the same electron and thereby realizes a self-coupled Landau-subband Hamiltonian. In the far-detuned regime, the cyclotron line acquires a state-dependent shift described by standard second-order perturbation theory. The resulting expression identifies the cyclotron resonance as a direct probe of the dynamical polarizability of the vertical ladder. The theory is intrinsically multilevel. Exact diagonalization confirms a broad microwave window in which sizable state-dependent cyclotron shifts are expected while the system remains dispersive.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the cyclotron resonance of an electron on liquid helium in a tilted magnetic field. The resonance shift is shown to act as a direct probe for the vertical polarizability of the electron's Rydberg-like subbands. By developing a full multilevel Hamiltonian and comparing it to simplified models, the authors map out the physical regimes where different theoretical approximations are valid.
main_problem: To use the cyclotron resonance of a surface-state electron on liquid helium as a direct, in situ spectroscopic probe of the dynamical polarizability of the electron's vertical Rydberg-like subbands.
main_result: The cyclotron resonance frequency shift is found to be proportional to the vertical susceptibility, confirming that the measurement probes the dynamical polarizability in a multilevel, self-coupled system.
method: The theory is developed from the microscopic tilted-field Hamiltonian, employing standard second-order perturbation theory to calculate the state-dependent shift.
model_or_system: The system is a single electron above liquid helium subjected to a tilted magnetic field and perpendicular electric field, leading to a self-coupled Landau-subband Hamiltonian.
key_observables: The cyclotron resonance frequency shift, $\delta\omega_c(m)$, and the differential splitting between cyclotron branches.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the far-detuned regime, comparing results across the two-subband limit, the full multilevel theory, and the near-resonant/hybridized regimes.
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve using second-order perturbation theory and comparing the full multilevel theory against the simplified two-subband truncation.
figures_summary: Figures compare multilevel theory, exact diagonalization, and the two-subband limit for cyclotron shifts across different field regimes, mapping out dispersive, crossover, and hybridized regions.
paper_structure: The paper develops the full multilevel Hamiltonian, derives the shift using perturbation theory, compares this result against exact diagonalization, and maps out the parameter space to delineate regimes where different approximations are valid.
why_interesting: This work models a complex, interacting quantum system (electron-helium interface) using concepts from cavity QED (resonance probing) and many-body physics (multilevel coupling), making it highly relevant to AMO physics.
